problem: Habitat-trained navigation agents are tested mostly in simulation, and prior Sim2Real work used a 3D-scanned replica of a simple, box-obstacle test room. Simulator-specific tricks such as wall sliding, plus sensor and actuation noise, cause a large Sim2Real gap.
motivation: Most researchers cannot afford billions of training frames or a 3D scan of their deployment site, so navigation should work as an out-of-the-box service in an unseen real environment. Simulator defaults (camera height, FoV, sliding physics, noiseless sensors) do not match a low-cost robot such as the LoCoBot, so a recipe is needed for transferring the agent.
key_idea: Adapt an occupancy-anticipation hierarchical PointNav agent for real-world deployment by removing simulator sliding, adding sensor noise, using wheel odometry instead of a learned pose estimator, and matching hyperparameters to the LoCoBot, then test it in an unseen multi-room office.
insight: Sim2Real transfer depends on details of the training setup, not only on architecture: blocking forward motion on collision, noisy sensors, depth hole-filling, and real-robot camera parameters. The real-world results show that transfer to an unseen scene is feasible for single-room or simple paths (A: SR 1.0), but it degrades when goals lie behind walls and no layout map exists (E: SR 0.2). The paper contains no ablation of the individual adaptations.
method: Baseline architecture: an occupancy anticipation agent with a mapper (ResNet-18 + U-Net producing egocentric and global 2-channel occupancy maps), a pose estimator, and a hierarchical policy (global policy, A* planner, local policy).
Hierarchical policy: the global goal is set to the navigation goal at test time. A* gives local goals within 0.25 m, and the local policy picks forward 25 cm or turn 15°.
Anti-trick training: the forward action is blocked when the bump flag is set, which emulates sticky surfaces and stops the agent from sliding along walls.
Sensor noise and depth restoration: Gaussian noise on RGB and Redwood noise on depth during training; on the real robot, Telea hole filling plus a median filter repair the RealSense depth.
Odometry replacement: the learned incremental pose estimator is replaced by LoCoBot wheel odometry, converted to episode-relative coordinates via A^-1.
Hyperparameter alignment: camera height 0.60 m, RGB FoV H70/V90, depth FoV H57/V86, depth range [0,5], obstacle height threshold [0.3,0.6]; PyRobot interfaces the sim code with the robot.
Training: PPO on Gibson in Habitat for 6.5M frames, with an anticipated-map-accuracy reward for the global policy and a distance-decrease minus collision-penalty reward for the local policy.

setting.backbone: Occupancy-anticipation style mapper (ResNet-18 + CNN + U-Net), pose/odometry, PPO hierarchical policy (trained from scratch in simulation)
setting.training_data: Gibson 3D scans in Habitat, 6.5M exploration frames with PPO; no real-world training data
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB-D from a single Intel RealSense camera plus wheel odometry
setting.action_space: Low-level: go forward 25 cm, turn 15° (global goal mapped to A* local goals)
setting.simulator: Habitat (Gibson scenes) for training; real-world LoCoBot for testing
setting.privileged: none (relative goal coordinates only; the agent has no map of the test scene, and memory is reset between episodes)

numbers.backbone: Occupancy-anticipation-based hierarchical agent trained in Habitat/Gibson
numbers.extra: Success = stop within 0.2 m; episode limit 300 steps; odometry from wheels; SPL normalized by steps

numbers_note: Per-path results for B, C and D are also in Table 2 but are not listed here. The test environment is a custom real-world office, not a standard benchmark.
results: On 50 real-world trials over 5 paths in an unseen multi-room office, LoCoNav achieves an overall SR of 0.6, SPL of 0.402, HFR of 0.14 and BR of 0.60. It reaches SR 1.0 on the single-room path A but only 0.2 on path E, where the goal lies behind an adjacent door. No baselines are compared.
limitations: No map of the layout, and PointNav goals lying behind walls force costly exploration; success drops to 0.2-0.5 on multi-room paths.
Only five paths in one office and no baseline or ablation comparisons, so the contribution of each adaptation is not quantified.
The high bump rate (0.60 overall, 1.0 on path E) and long episodes show weak collision avoidance.
compares_to: Kadian et al. Sim2Real Habitat-to-LoCoBot study (qualitative only)
